{"result":"## Authorization and capture
Payments authorizes when the order moves to pending and captures later, from the
capture worker, CAPTURE_DELAY_MINUTES after authorization. The delay exists so that
an order edited within a few minutes of checkout can be re-authorized without a
refund. The provider holds an authorization for AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES; a hold that
lapses before the worker captures produces E4021 on capture. Capture is idempotent
by order id, so a second capture of the same order returns E5011 and is treated as
success. Captures that fail with a retryable provider error are retried up to
MAX_CAPTURE_RETRIES times with exponential backoff.

## Service map
The platform is eight services behind one gateway. The gateway terminates TLS,
applies rate limits, and forwards to users, auth, orders, payments,
notifications, reporting, and search. Services call each other over internal
HTTP with the caller's session token forwarded only to the users and auth
services; every other internal call uses the calling service's own credential.
Orders calls payments to authorize and capture, payments calls notifications
when a capture succeeds or fails, and reporting reads a replica of the orders
and payments databases rather than calling either service.

## Order lifecycle
An order starts as a quote. Adding a payment authorization moves it to pending.
Capture moves it to paid. Only paid orders appear in revenue reports, which is why
the paid-total report filters on status rather than on the presence of a payment row.
A cancelled order keeps its rows; cancellation releases any inventory reservation
and voids an uncaptured authorization."}

structuredContent.result:
## Authorization and capture
Payments authorizes when the order moves to pending and captures later, from the
capture worker, CAPTURE_DELAY_MINUTES after authorization. The delay exists so that
an order edited within a few minutes of checkout can be re-authorized without a
refund. The provider holds an authorization for AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES; a hold that
lapses before the worker captures produces E4021 on capture. Capture is idempotent
by order id, so a second capture of the same order returns E5011 and is treated as
success. Captures that fail with a retryable provider error are retried up to
MAX_CAPTURE_RETRIES times with exponential backoff.

## Service map
The platform is eight services behind one gateway. The gateway terminates TLS,
applies rate limits, and forwards to users, auth, orders, payments,
notifications, reporting, and search. Services call each other over internal
HTTP with the caller's session token forwarded only to the users and auth
services; every other internal call uses the calling service's own credential.
Orders calls payments to authorize and capture, payments calls notifications
when a capture succeeds or fails, and reporting reads a replica of the orders
and payments databases rather than calling either service.

## Order lifecycle
An order starts as a quote. Adding a payment authorization moves it to pending.
Capture moves it to paid. Only paid orders appear in revenue reports, which is why
the paid-total report filters on status rather than on the presence of a payment row.
A cancelled order keeps its rows; cancellation releases any inventory reservation
and voids an uncaptured authorization.

content.text:
Staging is probably throwing E4021 because the authorization hold expires before the capture worker runs.

**What E4021 means:** "Payment authorization expired." The provider's hold on the payment lapsed before it was captured. It is **not retryable**: the fix is to re-authorize and then capture, not to retry the capture alone.

**How the timing works (from the architecture docs):** payments authorizes when an order moves to pending. The capture worker captures `CAPTURE_DELAY_MINUTES` later. The provider keeps the hold for `AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES`. If the hold lapses before the worker captures, the capture returns E4021.

**The likely misconfiguration** is in `config/staging/payments.conf`:

| Key | staging | production |
|---|---|---|
| `CAPTURE_DELAY_MINUTES` | 15 | 15 |
| `AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES` | **10** | 60 |

In staging the hold expires 10 minutes after authorization, but capture only starts at 15 minutes. So every capture will hit an expired hold and fail with E4021. Production works because its 60-minute hold outlasts the 15-minute delay. Either `AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES=10` in staging is a typo for 60, or something else needs to change so that `AUTH_HOLD_MINUTES` is clearly greater than `CAPTURE_DELAY_MINUTES` plus time for retries. With `MAX_CAPTURE_RETRIES=4` and exponential backoff, leave a margin. Also check what hold length the sandbox provider actually grants: if it really is 10 minutes, shorten the delay instead.

**Caveats:**
- I couldn't check the official config schema. `get_config_schema` was refused for insufficient scope (it needs `knowledge:read schema:read`), so I can't confirm these keys' defaults or allowed ranges. I compared staging against production instead.
- Nothing under `src/` mentions these keys or E4021, so the capture worker that reads them lives outside this repo. I haven't checked how it actually loads the values.

No files were edited.
